title: Stop Letting Others Pull Your Lever
author: Scott D. Clary
summary: Clary unpacks the advice 'become impossible to offend' by offering a practical map. Offense is a loss of control over your own response; the target wants to provoke a reaction and thus pull your lever. Becoming unshakeable is not about suppressing emotion but about creating a buffer between stimulus and response. He uses the egg-timer example: give yourself ten seconds between the provocation and your response, just long enough for the amygdala to settle and for rational thought to show up. In that gap lies your freedom. The shift is from reactive (others control you) to responsive (you choose your move). This is what it means to make peace with feedback, criticism, and insult: not by pretending they don't land, but by owning the space to decide what they mean.
points: Being offended means someone pulled your lever and got the reaction they wanted; the person who can't be rattled can't be controlled.
Becoming impossible to offend is not about suppressing emotions but about creating a buffer between stimulus and response, giving rational thought time to show up.
The egg-timer principle: ten seconds between provocation and response is enough time for your amygdala to settle, and for you to choose your move.
Offense handed to you is an invitation to react; you get to decide whether to accept it.
Your peace of mind is worth more than your need to be right.
quotes: Become impossible to offend. Let criticism bounce off, insults slide past, negativity flow through. The person who can't be rattled can't be controlled.

Your peace of mind is worth more than your need to be right. The art of not being rattled is about the gap between the stimulus and your response. In that gap lies your freedom.” Archived from Scott D. Clary Newsletter on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
